description: What PowerUp decides about one HTTP request head on its listener port (docs/protocol.md, "Connecting"). The head ends at the first CR LF CR LF or LF LF, whichever comes first (bare LF is tolerated, HK-254), and is read as UTF-8 with invalid bytes replaced; it splits into lines at LF, one trailing CR dropped from each. The request line splits on runs of spaces and needs a method and a target (the version is not read); the method is uppercased and the path is the target up to its first ?. A header line splits at its first colon; the name is trimmed of spaces and tabs and lowercased, the value trimmed; lines without a colon or with an empty name are skipped, and the last of two equal names wins. A request whose path is not exactly /ws is not a WebSocket request (plain HTTP handling carries on, HK-218). Otherwise, in order: a method other than GET is 405; an Upgrade value not containing websocket or a Connection value not containing upgrade (both lowercased) is 400 (HK-220); any Origin that is not empty once trimmed is 403 (HK-219); a Sec-WebSocket-Version other than exactly 13 is 426 (HK-221); a Sec-WebSocket-Key empty once trimmed is 400 (HK-222); else the upgrade is accepted with the accept key of the trimmed key (accept-key.json).
function: RequestHead.headerBoundary(in:), RequestHead(_:) and PowerUpProtocol.upgradeDecision(method:path:header:) — input the bytes received (a bytes descriptor), expected {"outcome": "incomplete"} (no header block yet), {"outcome": "unparseable"} (no request line; the listener answers 400), {"outcome": "notWebSocket", method, path}, {"outcome": "refuse", method, path, status, reason} or {"outcome": "accept", method, path, acceptKey}
